request.spec:
A rate may carry a to-date as well as a from-date (RATE_SET gains to=<date> at the end when one
was given; a to-date before the from-date is refused). A rate applies through its to-date; a claim
dated after the to-date of the rate that would apply to it, with no later rate in force on the
claim's date, has due n/a, and everything that reads due follows (a total skips it, a statement
binds n/a, the late charge has nothing to add to).
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A rate may carry a to-date as well as a from-date (RATE_SET gains to=<date> at the end when one
was given; a to-date before the from-date is refused). A rate applies through its to-date; a claim
dated after the to-date of the rate that would apply to it, with no later rate in force on the
claim's date, has due n/a, and everything that reads due follows (a total skips it, a statement
binds n/a, the late charge has nothing to add to).

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Rates can now have a to-date, and all 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass.

**What changed**
- **Stored data:** a new migration, `V27__rate_to.sql`, adds a `to_date` column to the rate table. A blank to-date means the rate never ends.
- **Server:**
  - A to-date that doesn't parse, or is before the from-date, is refused with a 400. Nothing is written to the store or the audit file.
  - `RATE_SET` adds ` to=<date>` at the end of the line when a to-date was given.
  - The two places that work out which rate applies, `RateRepository.find` and `Rollup.rateOn`, still pick the rate with the latest from-date. If the claim's date is after that rate's to-date, they now return no rate, so the claim's due is n/a. An earlier rate with no end date does not come back into force. Everything that reads due goes through these two, so the rollup and totals skip the claim, a statement binds n/a, and the late charge has nothing to add to.
- **Front end:** the rate form has a "To" field (`rate-form-to`), the rate list shows each rate's to-date (`rate-to`), and `rateOn` in `useRates.ts` follows the same rule as the server.

**One rule change you should check:** a person's due-total used to show n/a whenever their grade had no rate on the sheet's today. The test needs Ada's total to show 3.00 even though grade A has no rate today, because her earlier claims still have figures. So the total now also adds up when a claim dated on or before today still has a figure. A person with no such claims still shows n/a, which the audit expects. This doesn't change any existing result: before end dates, a claim on or before today with a rate always meant there was a rate today. I made this change in three places: `Rollup.snapshot`, `TakeStatement`, and `useDueTotals`.
